newsitem.title: USA: No one Euro centre to dominate at start - Deutsche.
newsitem.headline: No one Euro centre to dominate at start - Deutsche.

text.p: Europe's financial centres are likely to see considerable consolidation in coming years, once the single European currency, the Euro, is created, Deutsche Bank board member Rolf Breuer said.
But he added that no single financial centre was likely to be dominant in Euro trading, at least at first.
"There are 31 cash markets and 23 futures markets in Europe -- their existence is under threat," he said.
But he added that Frankfurt and Paris had already qualified to pass into the next round of tests.
"Both have tried to be very competitive. But the race has not taken place yet," he said. "I see these two competing at the start."
Breuer said it was obviously clear that London was making considerable efforts to pick up Euro business, even though the country may well not join the single currency at the start.
"I see London trying very hard to be a big player, also in the Euro," he said.
